gloss: Blue comes from indigo, meaning students surpass their teachers.
teaser: Ever wonder how students can sometimes outshine their teachers? Let's dive into this idiom!
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wonder how students can sometimes outshine their teachers? Let's dive into this idiom![break 1s] The phrase is: 青出于蓝, qīng chū yú lán.[break 0.5s] 青 (qīng) - blue or green[break 0.5s] 出 (chū) - to come out[break 0.5s] 于 (yú) - from[break 0.5s] 蓝 (lán) - indigo[break 1s] The full idiom again: 青出于蓝 literally means 'blue comes from indigo' and figuratively implies that students surpass their teachers.[break 1s] Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s] This idiom originates from ancient dyeing techniques where blue dye is made from the indigo plant. While the dye is blue, the plant itself is indigo. This highlights how the product can be more vibrant than its source, symbolizing how students can excel beyond their mentors. It beautifully captures the essence of growth and learning.[break 1.5s] Example 1: 他在音乐上青出于蓝。[break 1s] He has surpassed his teacher in music.[break 1s] Example 2: 这位年轻画家的作品青出于蓝。[break 1s] The works of this young artist surpass those of his teacher.[break 1s] Example 3: 她的表现青出于蓝，令人惊讶。[break 1s] Her performance surpassed expectations, leaving everyone amazed.[break 1s] So, 青出于蓝 means that students can surpass their teachers. Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
